title: What Survives When Activation Steering Is Used as Memory
abstract: arXiv:2610.14958v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Activation steering has recently been used as a memory for skills: past experiences of an agent are stored as steering vectors and retrieved later. Facts and preferences about the user are assumed to need text instead. We test that assumption with a training-free activation memory beside a frozen LLM. The change an experience causes in late-layer states is stored as a shift, filed under a whitened key for the conversation's gist, and added back in a later session only when the gist matches. We argue that such a shift is a fixed average of an effect that attention, in context, recomputes for every question, so only question-independent content can survive. In a pre-registered study on Qwen3.5-2B and 9B, with judges from four model families, the memory is selective (about 98% of unrelated replies are unchanged), but facts are stored as the word to say, in the last layers only, and are almost never used (at most 15% clean use, against 96-98

translated_title: 当激活引导被用作记忆时，什么能够存留
translated_abstract: 激活引导（activation steering）近来被用作技能的记忆：智能体过去的经验被存储为引导向量，以供日后检索。而关于用户的事实与偏好则被认为需要以文本形式存储。我们在一个冻结的大语言模型旁搭建了一个免训练的激活记忆来检验这一假设：一次经验在模型后层状态中引起的变化被存储为一个偏移量（shift），按对话主旨的白化键值归档，且仅在后续会话中主旨匹配时才被重新加回。我们论证，这样的偏移量本质上是注意力在上下文中针对每个问题重新计算的效应的固定平均值，因此只有与问题无关的内容才能存留。在一项针对 Qwen3.5-2B 和 9B 的预注册研究中，采用来自四个模型家族的评判模型，该记忆表现出选择性（约98%的无关回复保持不变），但事实被存储为“该说的词”，仅存在于最后几层，且几乎从未被使用（干净使用率至多15%，相比之下文本记忆为96–98……原文摘要在此截断）。
tldr: 该研究提出一种免训练的激活记忆机制，并证明激活引导偏移作为注意力效应的固定平均值只能存留与问题无关的内容：这种记忆虽具有约98%的高选择性，但用户事实仅被存储在最后几层且几乎从不被使用，表明用户事实与偏好仍需以文本形式记忆。
en_tdlr: Using a training-free activation memory beside a frozen LLM, this paper shows that steering-vector shifts—fixed averages of context-dependent attention effects—can only retain question-independent content: the memory is highly selective (~98% of unrelated replies unchanged), but user facts are stored only in the last layers and almost never used, indicating that facts and preferences still require text-based memory.
